The *Jarāsuttaniddesa* ("Exposition of the Discourse on Old Age", Mnd 6) is the sixth text of the *Mahāniddesa* in the Khuddaka Nikāya, providing a detailed word-by-word commentary and doctrinal exposition on the *Jarā Sutta* (Snp 4.6) of the Aṭṭhakavagga [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records two modern translations across two languages [SuttaCentral]. No direct discussions of the text were found in the sampled reference literature passages; however, its canonical framework and extensive textual connections are thoroughly documented in canonical listings and text-reuse data [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].

Curated passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral include the *Suttantikadukanikkhepa* of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* (Ds 2.3.3) and the *Guhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 2), alongside resembling parallels in other sections of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* (Ds 2.1.1, Ds 2.2.3) and the *Dutiyaāyusutta* (SN 4.10) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also notes cross-references or shared material in a wide array of canonical texts, including the *Kuha Sutta* (AN 4.26 / Iti 108), the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16), the *Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta* (DN 22), the *Alagaddūpama Sutta* (MN 22), the *Dhātuvibhaṅga Sutta* (MN 140), the *Salla Sutta* (Snp 3.8), the *Ñāṇakathā* (Ps 1.1), the *Saccavibhaṅga* (Vb 4), other *Niddesa* expositions (Mnd 14, Mnd 15), and the Jaina *Sūyagaḍaṅgasutta* [SuttaCentral].

Pali-internal text reuse analyzed by DharmaNexus records 3,207 matching passages across 151 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial internal reuse occurs with fellow *Niddesa* treatises—most heavily *Guhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 2, sharing 100 matches, including segments §3.2–20.1 ↔ §63.2–82.1), *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23, 126 matches), *Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 14, 109 matches), and *Attadaṇḍasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 15, 100 matches)—as well as the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), and the *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
